newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN CRIMINAL'S DEATH IN GREECE STRIKES CHORD.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN CRIMINAL'S DEATH IN GREECE STRIKES CHORD.

text.p: One of Russia's most notorious criminals has been found strangled in Greece, ending a short, brutal life that struck an alarming chord in a country weary of crime.
Alexander Solonik was one of a new generation of Russian criminals making a mark in western Europe and the United States.
Nicknamed Sasha the Macedonian for his habit of firing with both hands, known in Russia as "Macedonian style", he was wanted in Moscow for the murder of four policemen.
A Greek state coroner said Solonik, 37, a former police officer who had claimed responsibilty for a string of contract killings, was murdered on Saturday.
His body was found wrapped in garbage bags in a field in the northern Athens suburb of Varibobi.
Four Russian state security officers arrived in Athens on Saturday to search for Solonik and found his body in a joint search with local police, Greek officials said.
Russia's Sevodnya newspaper said the corpse's pockets were empty and he had no identification on him.
"On Saturday night it began to become apparent that the strangled man in Varibobi was none other than the legendary "Kurgan Rambo" Alexander Solonik, Russia's "Killer number one", Sevodnya said.

Solonik was born in the southern Russian city of Kurgan, east of the Ural mountain range, in 1960 to an intelligentsia family. A small, frail child, he became an expert in martial arts and marksmanship from an early age.
After military service he joined the police force but lasted only eight months before leaving. Two years later he was arrested and charged with rape but ecaped from custody.

He spent several months on the run before police caught him as he prepared to undergo plastic surgery to disguise his identity. He escaped from jail by squeezing through a ventilation shaft in the prison workshop.

In 1995 he allegedly opened fire on policemen trying to check his documents, using a gun hidden under a mackintosh draped over his arm. Four died and several others were injured in the shootout, in which Solonik was wounded in the kidney.
Interfax news agency said he still had a needle left in his body by doctors conducting an operation on the wound.
In his last escape from prison later the same year Solonik left a dummy in his bed and scaled a wall with a guard who had been bribed with money supplied by organised crime bosses.
The guard is still wanted by police.
Interfax quoted police sources as saying that Russian police, security services including the presidential security service had taken part in the operation along with Interpol to catch Solonik.
It was not known when he arrived in Greece, where police said Solonik was running a Russian mafia gang. He had been planning to travel to Italy this week, they said.

In recent years officials around the world have expressed fear that criminals from the former Soviet Union have successfully expanded their operations abroad since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991. The Russian mob's activities have included money laundering, fraud, drug dealing and murder.

A United States federal judge last month sentenced Vyacheslav Ivankov, the reputed "Godfather" of Russian organised crime in the United States, who was convicted of extortion and marriage fraud, to 115 months in prison.
